title: Charges Outside the Contract Sum Billed on the Reconstruction Final Draw
content:
The pass-through charges are the charge lines booked on a Reconstruction contract outside the current contract sum that the final draw bills.

**Carrier-funded.** A final draw is carrier-funded when its funding route, set by the base draw rule from the linked claim file, is not the customer: the claim file has a dwelling payment the carrier issued to the company directly (contractor direct), by a check naming the insured and the company (insured two-party), or into the mortgagee's loss-draft account (mortgagee loss draft). On any other final draw the customer funds the draw.

**Rule.**

- On a carrier-funded final draw of an insurance-claim contract: the permit fee, permit expediting, plan drawing, engineering letter, lead-safe setup and project management lines.
- On a self-pay contract: every charge line other than the contract sum, change order, overdue draw charge and remobilization lines, which a draw payment carries.
- On any other contract no charge line is added, and those lines are billed on the final invoice.

## Which lines are added

| Charge line on the contract | Carrier-funded final draw, insurance-claim contract | Self-pay contract | Insurance-claim contract whose final draw the customer funds |
|---|---|---|---|
| contract sum | no | no | no |
| change order | no | no | no |
| permit fee, permit expediting | yes | yes | no |
| plan drawing, engineering letter | yes | yes | no |
| lead-safe setup, project management | yes | yes | no |
| overdue draw charge, remobilization | no | no | no |

**Example (hypothetical figures).** A self-pay contract carries a permit fee line of $410.00, a permit expediting line of $160.00, an overdue draw charge of $42.50 and a remobilization line of $300.00: the final draw adds $570.00.
